column1: # Case-ID waivers for BaselineVerify.
# Lives in Tests/baseline/, not Tools/BaselineVerify/, deliberately: scripts/verify-baseline-log.ps1
# filters on Tests/baseline/*.tsv to require a "## Local regenerations" log entry (in
# Tests/baseline/baseline-*.env.txt) for any committed change under this directory, and a waiver
# is exactly the kind of change that needs the same append-only, reviewed record -- it excuses
# real differences from the frozen reference just as surely as a -FromLocal regeneration does,
# and previously could be added or edited with no forced record at all. There is no
# regenerate-baseline.ps1 mode that writes a waiver, so add the log entry by hand (same as a
# reference-mode version bump already requires) describing which waiver changed and why; see
# Tools/BaselineGen/README.md.
# Format: <glob>\t<PR-number>\t<reason>
# All three fields are required and non-empty; a malformed line is a hard load-time
# error, not a silent skip. See Tools/BaselineVerify/Waivers.cs for glob syntax ('*' is
# field-local, '**' crosses fields) and why "*"/"**" and anything matching the synthetic
# probe case id are rejected outright.
# Every waiver is checked for staleness at the end of a run: if it matched zero rows,
# or every row it matched was byte-for-byte identical anyway, the run fails. A waiver
# that isn't earning its keep is worse than no waiver: it's coverage nobody is
# looking at. Add a waiver in the same PR that needs it, and delete it in the PR that
# makes it unnecessary -- do not leave it behind "just in case".
# No entries at the moment: intentionally empty.
